project_goal: Provide a private, local-first news aggregator that collects selected sources and ranks the most relevant articles first for one user on Windows 11.
target_users: The repository owner as the sole local user

mvp.summary: A manually launched Windows executable serves an installable web application that ingests configured news sources, ranks articles locally, and supports a persistent personal reading workflow.
must_have: Ship an installable progressive web application with Windows 11 as the first supported platform.
Launch as one Windows executable that starts the local server and opens the application in the default browser.
Provide a small editable starter catalog and allow manual source configuration.
Ingest RSS/Atom feeds, supported official news APIs, and explicitly approved public-page scrapers.
Rank articles using transparent weighted rules plus lightweight local text similarity such as TF-IDF or BM25.
Prioritize explicit interests, selected sources, recency, and reading actions over optional low-weight demographic signals.
Keep the user profile, article data, ranking data, and semantic processing on the local machine.
Let the user manually select a coarse location and optionally provide age, gender, and city; every demographic field must be optional and disableable.
Explain concisely why each article received its position.
Display full article content in-app only when the feed or source permissions provide it; otherwise display metadata and link to the publisher.
Support read/unread state, save-for-later, hide/dismiss, and basic filtering.
Persist sources, articles, settings, ranking data, and library state across restarts in SQLite.
Store optional API credentials in Windows Credential Manager through a replaceable credential-storage interface.
postponed: User accounts, synchronization, and multi-user support
Bundled embedding models or separately installed local model services
Folders, annotations, exports, and cross-article research features
Background-service installation, automatic startup, and ingestion while the executable is closed
Broad scraping or any access-control, paywall, login, or rate-limit bypass

target_platforms: Installable progressive web application served on localhost

stack.preference: Go as the main backend, Vue with TypeScript as the SPA frontend, and SQLite for local persistence.
stack.recommendation: Embed the compiled Vue SPA into the Go executable, keep ranking and ingestion behind replaceable interfaces, and use lightweight local text similarity for the MVP.

options.name: Selected: Go + Vue + TypeScript + SQLite
options.best_for: A local-first interactive PWA distributed as one Windows executable.
risks: The frontend adds a separate build toolchain.
Windows Credential Manager integration requires platform-specific code.
PWA installation behavior depends on browser support.

options.name: Postponed: bundled local embedding runtime
options.best_for: Stronger semantic matching without sending data off-device.
risks: More complex native Windows packaging and runtime management.

notes: The repository was empty before the initial README commit and framework bootstrap.

tools.name: Windows Credential Manager
tools.configuration: Access through a replaceable Go credential-storage interface.
tools.notes: Store optional news API keys without plaintext application configuration.

team_mode.parallelization_goal: Allow two implementation agents to work concurrently after shared contracts are established, with a third independent reviewer agent gating every implementation pull request.

working_style.review_style: Every implementation pull request requires automated checks and explicit reviewer-agent approval; a rejection blocks merging until resolved.
proof_required: Relevant Vue unit or component tests
A critical-path browser test where applicable
Lint and build checks for affected components

constraints: The application is for one local user and will not publish or redistribute aggregated content.
The MVP must operate without external AI or embedding services.
The local server and ingestion run only while the manually launched executable is open.
Ranking must remain explainable and demographic influence must be optional, disableable, and low-weight.
The application must preserve a clean adapter boundary for future ingestion and semantic-ranking upgrades.
safety_boundaries: Scrape only public pages whose terms and robots guidance permit automated access.
Do not bypass paywalls, authentication, access controls, rate limits, or publisher restrictions.
Display full content in-app only when the source feed or permissions provide it; otherwise link to the publisher.
Keep profile and article-processing data local and do not send it to external AI services.
Do not store API credentials in plaintext application data.
Do not infer sensitive demographic fields; collect only optional values explicitly entered by the user.
assumptions: The sole user controls the Windows 11 machine and local application data.
Manual refresh and refresh-while-running are sufficient for the MVP.
Starter sources can be changed without an application release.
Browser storage is limited to disposable UI preferences or caches; SQLite is authoritative.
Coarse location is sufficient for regional news relevance.

open_questions.question: Which feeds and regions should make up the initial starter catalog?
open_questions.risk_if_unanswered: A placeholder catalog can be used during implementation, but final onboarding usefulness cannot be evaluated.

open_questions.question: Which official news APIs and approved scraper targets should be implemented first?
open_questions.risk_if_unanswered: The MVP can prove adapter behavior with RSS and fixtures, but provider-specific acceptance cannot be completed.

open_questions.question: What initial weights should each ranking signal use?
open_questions.risk_if_unanswered: Planning can define configurable defaults, but ranking quality will require user tuning after real usage.

acceptance_signals: The user can build or obtain the Windows executable, launch it manually, and open the locally served PWA.
The user can configure a local profile and sources without creating an account.
A refresh ingests articles from configured sources and produces a relevance-ranked feed.
Each ranked article presents a concise explanation based on enabled signals.
The user can read permitted content in-app or open the publisher link.
Read, saved, hidden, filtering, profile, and source state persist across restarts.
Optional API credentials are stored through Windows Credential Manager.
Layered automated checks and a Windows build smoke check pass.
The independent reviewer agent approves the implementation pull request.
